entries.title: Sharp recovery from two tensor block symmetries
entries.statement: Let H,W be finite-dimensional real Hilbert spaces and 1<=p<=q. If T in H^(tensor(p+q)) tensor W is invariant under permutations of its first p positions and, separately, of its next q positions, and P_q averages permutations of the first q positions, then ||T||<=binom(q,p)||P_qT||. The constant is optimal for dim H>=2 and W nonzero. Norms are the induced Hilbert tensor norms.
entries.proof_text: Associate to each p-subset F a permuted tensor T_F. Double expansion and Vandermonde give sum_{|E|=q}||sum_{F subset E}T_F||^2=sum_{s=0}^p binom(q-p,p-s)sum_{|S|=s}||sum_{F superset S}T_F||^2. The s=p term is sum_F||T_F||^2; all terms are nonnegative. Each left sum is binom(q,p) times a permutation of P_qT, proving the bound. For sharpness, in a two-dimensional orthonormal basis set the tensor component with p total ones and r ones in the first block to (-1)^r/binom(q,p-r), and all others to zero. A kth alternating binomial difference shows P_qT=(-1)^p RT/binom(q,p) for a block reversal R. Thus equality is attained. A separate disjointness-operator proof is saved in w350 reviews/w348_independent.md.

entries.title: Exact normalized tilt norm for exponential products
entries.statement: Let X_i=Y_i-1 for independent rate-one exponential Y_i, 1<=i<=n, and let mu be their joint law. For F_f(z)=E[f(X)e^(z.X)]/E[e^(z.X)] and T_d f=(1/d!)D^dF_f(0), using the ordered-index Hilbert-Schmidt norm, the operator norm from L^2(mu) to HS tensors is sqrt(binom(2d-2,d-1)) for every d>=1 and n>=1. The smallest base R valid in ||T_d f||<=R^d||f||_2 for all degrees is 2.
entries.proof_text: The tilt kernel is product_i(1-z_i)e^(z_iY_i). Its coefficients P_0=1 and P_j=y^j/j!-y^(j-1)/(j-1)! are centered for j>=1 and satisfy E[P_jP_k]=binom(j+k-2,j-1). Ordered multiplicities give ||T_df||^2=sum_{|alpha|=d}(alpha!/d!)|<f,product P_alpha_i>|^2. Distinct coordinate supports are orthogonal by independence and centering. For one support of size s, the frame norm is at most its trace, bounded by binom(2(d-s),d-s)sum alpha!/d!. The factorial/composition bound sum alpha!/d!<=(d-s+1)/(d(s-1)!)<=1, so every block norm is <=binom(2d-2,d-1). Orthogonality means the maximum of block norms, with no support-count factor. The test f=P_d(Y_1)/sqrt(binom(2d-2,d-1)) attains equality. Central binomial bounds between 4^(d-1)/(2d-1) and 4^(d-1) give optimal base 2. This is a product special case, not general log-concavity.

entries.title: Quadratic moment operator, variance duality and the tilt domain
entries.statement: Let mu be centered and isotropic in R^n with finite fourth moments. Define the bounded quadratic-moment operator U_2 f=(1/2)E[f(X)(XX^T-I)]. Its L^2-to-Hilbert-Schmidt norm equals (1/2)sup_{A=A^T,||A||_HS=1}sqrt(Var_mu(X^TAX)). If mu additionally satisfies E exp(epsilon|X|)<infinity for some epsilon>0, then F_f(z)=E[f(X)e^(z.X)]/E[e^(z.X)] is defined near zero for every L^2 f and U_2 f=(1/2)D^2F_f(0). The local exponential moment is needed for this derivative identification and is automatic for log-concave laws; no uniform radius is asserted.
entries.proof_text: Pair U_2 f with an HS-unit symmetric A. The functional is half the covariance with X^TAX, and its L2 norm is half the standard deviation. Interchanging the two suprema proves the identity; a normalized centered quadratic attains every nonzero-variance functional norm. Antisymmetric matrices pair to zero. Under E exp(epsilon|X|)<infinity, for |z|<epsilon/4 Cauchy-Schwarz bounds derivatives using E[|X|^4 exp(2|z||X|)]<infinity. Differentiate the quotient twice: mean zero removes the first-order denominator terms, covariance I gives D^2F_f(0)=E[f(XX^T-I)]. Finite fourth moments alone do not define the quotient, as independently checked polynomial-tail counterexamples show.
assumptions: Finite fourth moments for the algebraic U_2 identity
Local exponential moment only for identification with a tilt derivative

entries.title: Posterior variances cannot be factored in expectation
entries.statement: Let X=Exp(1)-1, s>0, and Y=sX+sqrt(s)Z for independent standard Gaussian Z. Write A(Y)=Var(X|Y). Then E[A(Y)^2]>(E[A(Y)])^2. In particular, for fixed f(x)=x, the bound E|Cov(f(X),X|Y)|^2<=(E||Cov(X|Y)||_op)(E Var(f(X)|Y)) is false, even for this isotropic log-concave prior and genuine Gaussian observation.
entries.proof_text: The posterior density is proportional to exp((y-1)x-sx^2/2) on x>=-1, a truncated Gaussian with variance A(y). At y=1-s it is a half-normal translated to -1, with variance (1-2/pi)/s. As y tends to positive infinity the truncation disappears and A(y) tends to 1/s. The variance is continuous, so it is nonconstant; Y has positive density everywhere. Strong log-concavity gives 0<A(y)<=1/s, so A(Y) is square integrable and Var(A(Y))>0. The proposed inequality is exactly the reverse of this strict variance identity. No assertion about a correctly weighted estimate or a full KLS proof follows.
